bench_run_1791530447_16.content: How is Employee Provident Fund (EPF) calculated on my monthly salary slip?

Employee Provident Fund (EPF) is calculated based on the basic salary and certain allowances in your monthly salary slip. Here is a breakdown of how it typically works:

• Contribution Rate: Both the employee and employer contribute a certain percentage of the employee's basic salary plus dearness allowance (if applicable) to the EPF account. The standard rates are usually:
  • Employee: 12%
  • Employer: 12% (with 8.33% going towards the Employee Pension Scheme and 3.67% directly to EPF)

• Calculating EPF: The EPF contribution is calculated as follows:
  • EPF Contribution = (Basic Salary + Dearness Allowance) × 12% 

• Employer Contribution: The employer's contribution is split into:
  • 8.33% for the Employee Pension Scheme (EPS)
  • 3.67% for EPF

• Monthly Salary Slip: On your salary slip, you will see two entries related to EPF:
  • Your contribution to EPF 
  • The employer's contribution to EPF & EPS
